card.name: Just before a drug's effect is stated
card.fires_on: The word or word ending right after a drug or drug class name, just before the label says what it does (e.g. 'can prolong', 'slow conduction', 'cause'). It also fires on the ending of drug names such as beta-blockers and insulins.

modes.label: Drug class ending
modes.description: The plural ending of a drug class or drug name that is the subject of a warning.

modes.label: Linking word before an effect
modes.description: A verb or preposition after a drug name that leads into an effect or a shift of a substance.
modes.example: Ketoconazole<< can>> prolong the QT interval.

card.plain: It marks the spot right after a drug is named, where the label is about to say what the drug does.
